note: Same company: Banyan Systems of Westborough, Massachusetts, renamed ePresence in 1999. ePresence sold its services business (customer relationships, partnerships and most employees) to Unisys and its Switchboard stake to InfoSpace, both closed by 2004-06-04, and then dissolved under its plan of liquidation (ePresence 8-K exhibit 99.1, 2004-06-04). The business carried on under a buyer, so the asset-sale rule reads acquired, as Battery and Sutter Hill already have it; Greylock's defunct is stale. Greylock also holds the same company a second time as its epresence row, and Sequoia's epresence row, both read defunct on the same facts.

note: Same company: Khosla's row is Faire Wholesale, Inc. (Form D CIK 1763016, Keith Rabois named as director in 2018 while at Khosla), the San Francisco wholesale marketplace Lightspeed, Sequoia and Y Combinator (W17) hold. A November 2025 tender led by WCM Investment Management valued it at $5.2B (Digital Commerce 360, 2025-12-05; Bloomberg reported the employee share sale on 2025-11-17); no later priced event was found (the September 2026 'Faire files for ACE Market IPO' item is a Malaysian namesake). Khosla's below_1b was never web-checked and is stale. This one Khosla alignment settles both the Lightspeed and the Sequoia pair, and also the Y Combinator pair (y-combinator:faire already reads private, 1b_plus, $5.2B as of 2025-11-17 from the same source). Lightspeed's own valuation_citation is sacra.com, a vendor page (Rule A); the tender's press source should replace it.

note: Same company: KupiVIP, the Moscow private-shopping e-commerce site both firms backed in its 2010 to 2012 rounds. Yandex agreed in June 2021 to buy its assets and withdrew in July (Reuters, 2021-07-09); KupiVIP then shut down on 2021-09-01 with no sale (The Moscow Times, 2021-09-08). Balderton's defunct is right; Accel's acquired rests on an unsourced 'consolidation 2021' note and is stale.

align.note: KupiVIP shut down on 2021-09-01 after Yandex withdrew in July 2021 from buying its assets, and no sale followed (The Moscow Times, 2021-09-08).

note: Same company: Spark's row is Plume Design (Form D CIK 1664759, Todd Dagres as director, plumewifi.com), the Palo Alto smart-home WiFi company whose 2021 Series E Insight led. The row's identity is mixed: it describes Plume Design, but its below_1b and its PitchBook range citation were judged on a homonym (the RWA blockchain PLUME token) whose text leaked into the note. Plume Design's last priced round is the $300M round led by SoftBank Vision Fund 2 at $2.6B (TechCrunch, 2021-10-12); it still operates privately (it bought Sweepr in January 2026). Insight's $1.35B (Series E, February 2021, cited from Insight's own post) is superseded by the same October 2021 mark; its band is unchanged. Y Combinator's plume (plumefinder.com, Paris, S24) is a different company and must not carry this band.

note: Two different companies that share a name. Sequoia's Root, Inc. is Root Insurance of Columbus, Ohio (Form D CIK 1637429, Nasdaq ROOT since 2020); Insight's Root is the former Slim.AI of Boston, a container-security company whose 2022 Series A Insight led. Different founders, product and city. Separately, the Sequoia row's only membership evidence is a 2018 Form D naming Christopher Olsen, who left Sequoia in 2012 to co-found Drive Capital, an early Root backer, so Sequoia's membership in Root Insurance looks wrong and wants a review.

Two different companies that share a name. Sequoia's Versatile was on Sequoia's company pages by October 2006, among its older holdings, and its row says it is unidentified. Insight's is versatile.ai, the construction-site analytics company whose first Form D (CIK 1834016) is the November 2020 Series A Insight led; it did not exist when Sequoia listed its Versatile.

Same company: Yubi (formerly CredAvenue), the Chennai debt marketplace; Lightspeed backed it from the 2021 Series A and is named among its backers in the Series B coverage. The $137M Series B of March 2022 valued it at $1.3B (TechCrunch, 2022-03-06); the November 2025 Rs 411 crore round was founder equity plus debt with no valuation disclosed. Lightspeed's below_1b is stale. Insight's $1.5B comes from a 2023 secondary sale by the parent Vivriti, reported second-hand; the valuation rule keeps secondary figures in the note, so Insight's figure should read the $1.3B primary too (the band is the same either way).
